A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LEG guardrail study. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support comparison, including matching the relocated joint-loss ablation.

before.justification: v1 reports original LEG classification results, faithfulness tests, ablations, efficiency measurements, and human-label evaluations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds explanation-label coverage experiments, a labeling-strategy comparison, and additional baseline and false-positive results.

M1.justification: The shared encoder, attention pooling, classification heads, opposing-query annotation procedure, and uncertainty-weighted losses remain unchanged. Appendix D's explicit zero explanation loss for unlabeled instances clarifies the prompt-only training already described in v1.

E1.justification: Both versions use AEGIS2.0, WildGuardMix, ToxicChat0124, XSTest, human-annotated subsets, and withheld-risk-topic evaluations. The new supervision-coverage and jury-labeling experiments reuse existing datasets and tasks.

E2.justification: v2 adds GuardReasoner 1B, 3B, and 8B to Table 1's accuracy comparisons, a three-LLM jury labeling alternative in Appendix K, and Prompt Baseline variants to the XSTest comparison. GuardReasoner's earlier participation in efficiency comparisons does not duplicate its new accuracy evaluation.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs vary explanation supervision through randomly selected 20%, 40%, 60%, and available higher-coverage conditions, and train LEG with labels requiring agreement among three specified LLMs. XSTest additionally reports false-positive rate. Existing main-experiment training settings and evaluation splits are unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendices D and K investigate sensitivity to explanation-label availability and an alternative labeling strategy. XSTest gains a single-task comparison of false positives. These substantially extend the analysis; the joint-loss ablation itself is unchanged and merely moves from Appendix F to Section 5.4.

E5.justification: Both retain seeds 42, 52, and 62, mean and standard deviation reporting in the main LEG comparisons, and the same human-agreement assessment. No changed repeated-run policy, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedure is introduced.

E6.justification: Original LEG scores remain unchanged, but v2 adds substantial results for GuardReasoner, supervision coverage, jury labeling, and XSTest baselines/FPR. Table 9 adds jury-trained LEG-large's 52.08 F1 on human-annotated AEGIS against the retained 66.11 with proposed labels. Table 13 adds FPRs of 1.6 for WildGuardMix-trained LEG-large and 6.4 for its Prompt Baseline counterpart.

T1.justification: The joint-loss equations, polarization-score definitions, attention-pooling and classifier formulas, and lexical-similarity definition are unchanged. No new theorem, proof, or substantive mathematical derivation appears.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about lightweight explainable guardrails, synthetic supervision, the joint loss, and competitive in-domain and out-of-domain performance. Their wording changes do not alter scientific scope.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations that roughly 40% explanation supervision suffices, the proposed labeling approach aligns better with human judgments than the tested jury, and joint training usually reduces XSTest false positives. These refine the existing account; the multilingual limitation and earlier interpretations remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds code and model/dataset access links, explicitly documents zeroing the explanation loss when labels are unavailable, and acknowledges DGX Spark computational support. The existing architecture descriptions, annotation algorithm, and main hyperparameters remain.

R1.justification: v2 supplies the Kang and Li (2025) citation for the previously discussed R2-Guard and expands the Constitutional AI description to mention AI-feedback training. The broader related-work coverage and novelty positioning remain stable.

P1.justification: Most prose and organization are retained. The loss ablation moves into Section 5.4, new appendices are integrated, headings and wording receive limited edits, and acceptance and acknowledgment text is added.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 5 and 9, expands Table 1 and the XSTest table, moves the ablation table into the main text, and enlarges the faithfulness display. Figure 1(b)'s example is aligned with the architecture illustration, and Figure 2's caption is clarified. The overall visual format remains consistent.

improvement.justification: The added supervision-coverage analysis, stronger comparisons, XSTest false-positive measurements, and resource links improve validation and reproducibility. The gains are limited: Appendix K changes teacher models together with the labeling procedure, weakening causal attribution, and Section 5.1 still calls WildGuard best despite Table 1's newly reported GuardReasoner score of 89.02 versus 88.9. The revision strengthens an otherwise largely unchanged paper.
